assessment.title: Arrays — Section-End Assessment
assessment.description: 12 MCQs. Passing threshold 70% is required alongside 10/12 problems completed to unlock Strings.

questions.text: For an array `arr` of length n (0-indexed), the last element is accessed as:
questions.explanation: The valid indices are 0..n-1, so the last is arr[n-1].

options: Indices of two numbers that add up to a target
The two identical elements of an array
questions.explanation: Given nums and target, return the indices i,j with nums[i] + nums[j] = target.
Each output element is the sum of all input elements up to and including that index.

questions.text: The 'Contains Duplicate' problem returns true when:
options: Some value appears at least twice
questions.explanation: Presence of any duplicated value constitutes a duplicate.

questions.text: After moving all zeroes of [0, 1, 0, 3, 12] to the end while preserving the order of non-zero elements, the result is:
questions.explanation: Only zeros are moved to the end; the relative order of 1, 3, 12 is preserved.

questions.text: For prices [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4], the maximum profit achievable by one buy followed by one later sell is:
questions.explanation: Buy at 1 and sell at 6 gives a profit of 5.

questions.text: The in-place 'remove duplicates from sorted array' algorithm uses which invariant?
options: Two pointers: one scans, one marks the write position for unique values
questions.explanation: Because the array is sorted, the write pointer only advances when a new distinct value is encountered.

questions.text: Using Kadane's algorithm on [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4], the maximum subarray sum is:
questions.explanation: The subarray [4, -1, 2, 1] achieves the maximum sum of 6.

questions.text: For 'Number of Good Pairs' on the array [1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 3], the count of pairs (i < j) with nums[i] = nums[j] is:
questions.explanation: Three 1s contribute C(3,2) = 3 pairs; two 3s contribute C(2,2) = 1 pair; total 4.

questions.text: For 'Find Numbers with Even Number of Digits' on [12, 345, 2, 6, 7896], the count of qualifying numbers is:
questions.explanation: 12 (two digits) and 7896 (four digits) are even-length; the others are odd-length.

questions.text: The best achievable time complexity for the unsorted 'Two Sum' problem, with no constraints on extra space, is:
options: O(n), using a hash map (average case)
questions.explanation: A single pass stores each value and looks up target minus value in the hash map, giving expected O(n).

questions.text: In Kadane's algorithm, the invariant maintained at each index is:
options: current_sum tracks the sum of the entire array so far
current_sum tracks the maximum subarray sum ending at the current index; max_sum tracks the overall maximum
current_sum equals max_sum at every step
questions.explanation: current_sum is reset to the current element when it would be smaller than the running sum, while max_sum stores the best seen so far.
